testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: Verify branch is rebased on base (needs pull-request context and full git history, not the worktree); Validate renovate.json (fetches renovate from the npm registry via npx on every run); smoke-omp (needs bun and a globally installed pinned omp binary); install-and-smoke (needs bun and a globally installed pinned omp binary).

survived.claim: The new staticImport quoted-name alternative `"(?:[^"\\\n]|\\.)*"` cannot read a string-named specifier holding a line continuation (backslash + LF, CRLF or U+2028), so `import { "C\<LF>FG" as C } from "./common.mjs"` — which Node resolves to the export CFG — is neither read by the line-start reader (its clause holds a quote) nor refused, and a write `C.ms = <env read>` through it is silently accepted with problems [] and reaches [].

votes.reason: Ran the snapshot copy's exact staticImport regex (tests/gh-spawn-bound.test.mjs:329). For `import { "C\<LF>FG" as C } from "./common.mjs"` (also CRLF and U+2028 variants) exec returns no match, so the refusal path (line 333 `?.[3]`) never fires; the plain `"CFG"` control matches ./common.mjs. Node accepts the continuation form: `node y.mjs` with `C.ms=1; console.log(C.ms)` printed 1, exit 0. This confirms the regex gap. I did not rerun the full sweep to see problems [] (I relied on the claim's probe output for that), but no other refusal appears in the surrounding code I read. CWD-AUDIT: dirty /Users/chris/dev/fleet-plugin — untracked docs/metrics/runs/2026-11-20T165122Z/{closeout.json,ledger.md,phase0.json,plugin-version}; I wrote nothing there, those are controller files.

The regex gap is real. I ran the new staticImport regex in node on `import { "C\<LF>FG" as C } from "./common.mjs"`: it returns false (no match), while the plain `import { "CFG" as C } ...` control returns true. `\\.` cannot consume a backslash followed by a line terminator. The diff shows the line-start reader was also changed to exclude quotes in its clause (`[^}"']*`), so neither reader handles this case. I did not rebuild the copy or rerun the PROBE test, so the claim's `problems: []` output rests on the finding's evidence and my reading of the diff, not my own run. No other handling of this case appears in the diff. This is a narrow gap; the regex observation supports the claim only up to the unmatched import. CWD-AUDIT: not run; this cell only read files and ran a stateless node -e in /tmp. The checkout at /Users/chris/dev/fleet-plugin was never modified.

unverified.claim: The new comment says the quoted-name alternatives read escapes 'as one character each', but the pattern `\\.` consumes a backslash plus one following character, so `\u0043` is read as `\u` followed by plain characters, not as one unit.
unverified.evidence: The staticImport regex at lines ~325-329 uses `"(?:[^"\\\n]|\\.)*"`. The `\\.` alternative matches exactly two characters. `\u0043` is six characters and is read as `\u` then `0043`. The result is still correct: the unicode-escape test case is refused.
unverified.suggested_fix: Reword to 'a backslash and the character after it are read as a pair', or 'a backslash escapes the next character'.
